type_why: Cheerful and restless is Lola exactly: up at 4:30 humming, can't stand a quiet room, restless when nobody needs her, organised the hospital ward. 'You can skip past what is wrong' fits how she decides each morning not to think about her son. The type's trap is wrong for her, though. 'Pleasure... one more helping, one more episode' is nothing like a widow who lends her last peso. Her trap, as Tessie sees it, is needing to be needed.

links.link: Speaks up: idle talk slides, step by step, into talk about other people
links.why: She complains about her son to everyone except him. Tessie would nod at this one.

links.link: Open-handed: giving so much at once that they run short and start grumbling; counsel 'do not keep score'
links.why: This is her weighing exactly: the 30,000 pesos lent for a motorbike, now needed for her own medicine. It also hits what the friend sees, 'mention it to you, kindly, for the next ten years', and the score she says she never keeps.

links.link: Light-hearted: pleasure sits right next door to cheerfulness
links.why: This repeats the type's trap almost word for word. Nothing in her life or her friend's view points to pleasure as the pull.

links.link: You let rudeness go, then hours later think of what you should have said (the evening after)
links.why: It catches the quiet 'It's okay, anak' and the list of the ungrateful that lives in her head for years. One part misfits: 'wishing you had been harsher' is not quite her. She goes cold. She does not wish she had been harsh.

links.link: You let things slide and calm friends down: keeping the peace can be the easier road
links.why: She won't ask the nephew for the money and won't say it to her son's face. The report never names either, but she would see it.

links.link: Kindred: Augustine as a young man, lover of talk and jokes, honest about where pleasure led
links.why: It's the type's fixed kindred. A young man's pleasures sit oddly on a devout 67-year-old widow.

fight_should_be: Vainglory, the need to be needed and thanked: she mentions a gift for ten years and keeps a list of who never said thank you. Anger held as quiet resentment comes a close second. Listlessness also has a claim, in the narrow sense of putting off the hard conversation. 'I put off the one thing that matters most' was her highest private answer (the nephew, her son), yet it was ranked third, below gluttony, which she said happens rarely.
line_why: The Host is her: pancit sent to a wake, feeding the family, a sari-sari store in the front window. She picked it herself, and her friend would agree.
leanings_wrong: Candour: 'Says it plainly'. When she is hurt she goes quiet and says 'It's okay, anak' in a voice that means it isn't, and she tells everyone but her son what she thinks of him. Her friend would put her on 'Chooses what to show'.
When wronged: 'Lets it go (83/100)'. That is true in the moment only. Her friend knows the list she keeps for years, so the label reads as a verdict she has not earned.
wording_issues: 'How your anger works: Slow and brief... it does not last... Keep it that way' confirms her self-image against her friend's view, and it contradicts the report's own 'evening after' link. The p02 report hedged with 'Ask someone close to you whether they agree'. This one did not, though she answered 'Sometimes' to replaying what people did.

The fight leads with Gluttony although she answered 'rarely' to eating or drinking to take the edge off. This is a scoring artefact: a single-item thought is drawn toward the middle, which lifts a low answer, and 'Enjoys comforts' adds to it. Her strongest private answer, putting off the thing that matters most, came third. 'No single one leads' is honest, but the full gluttony page that follows still reads as the verdict.

'Give steadily and cheerfully, and do not keep score' could read, for a poor widow who needs her loan back for blood-pressure medicine, as a hint that asking for it is score-keeping. That brushes the round-2 rule of no scolding of the generous poor.
The pleasure-next-door point appears twice, in the type and in the Light-hearted leaning.
Seven help lines is long for a phone. They are all fine, though.
best_moment: The Open-handed reading: Gregory warns the generous against giving so much at once that they run short and start grumbling. Then comes 'do not keep score'. That is the 30,000-peso loan, the medicine she now can't afford, and the ten years of kindly reminders, all in two sentences she had never put into words.
worst_moment: The private fight opens on Gluttony ('Reaching for food or drink to take the edge off') for a woman who said she rarely does. It sits beside a type trap of 'one more helping, one more episode' and an anger section that tells her to 'keep it that way'. Together they miss the needing-to-be-needed and the list of the ungrateful that her friend sees first.

type_why: Quick, funny, restless and hating to wait is the Marcus his mates see. 'You can skip past what is wrong' is his 'no hard feelings, yeah?'. The pleasure trap ('one more thing you enjoy a little too much') lands squarely on the four or five cans until noon. But 'your mood runs light... things rarely get you down' misses the days of silence and the drinking. His friend's first word about him is the fuse, not cheerfulness. The fuse only shows up in the strongest leanings line.

links.link: Lets them know: impatience can wreck in one moment what took years to build
links.why: The divorce and Ellie's trust. His weighing is her question about the shouting.

links.link: Fiery: the hot-tempered mistake their anger for righteousness
links.why: It punctures his self-view of 'honest and straightforward, says what everyone else is thinking'.

links.link: Takes a stand: quarrels grow from pride in a gift that sets us apart, like knowing more or trying harder
links.why: Nothing about Marcus suggests pride in knowing more. His stands come from heat and loyalty.

links.link: You let people know on the spot, and you snap and wish you hadn't: the care arrives too late
links.why: It fits the can from the machine ten minutes later, and the hot flash of shame at Ellie's eyes in the mirror.

links.link: You tell people in charge they're wrong, and your anger feels justified: honesty can be pride, zeal can be temper
links.why: It's accurate, but it reuses the exact quote from the Fiery leaning.

links.link: Type trap: pleasure, 'it looks like a good time'
links.why: 'Winding down' with cans and football highlights is exactly a temptation that doesn't look like one. He denies the drinking, and this names it without accusing him.

links.link: Kindred: young Augustine
links.why: The pleasure-honesty part fits the drinking. 'Friendly arguments' does not describe his arguments.

fight_should_be: Gluttony is right: in private he admitted drinking to take the edge off, and Dean says it is worse than he admits. Anger second is right too. The page could say more plainly that drink is the fuel for the rest (no sleep after nights, then a short fuse). Cassian's 'break your own fast gladly for a guest' is noise for him.
line_why: The Advocate fits a man who would square up to anyone who disrespected his mates and who covers breaks unasked. He picked it both times.
leanings_wrong: Seen and unseen: 'Better in private (75/100)'. His best is on the warehouse floor, where he knows whose mum is poorly. At home Ellie walks on eggshells. His friend would put him on the other side.
Mood: 'Light-hearted'. This is his self-image. His friend knows the low spells, the days of ignored messages and the drinking.
wording_issues: Nothing tells him how he lands on people. Dean's central point, 'no idea how frightening he is... people walk on eggshells round him, Ellie included', goes unsaid. The signal was there: he answered c1 at the extreme, 'I don't always notice I've upset someone until they tell me'. The quiz uses that item only as a correction preference ('Say it straight'). Paired with his fast anger, it would have given the aha he most needs, and the answer to Ellie's question.

The same point, anger passing itself off as zeal or righteousness, is made three times. The Fiery leaning and the second link share one quote, and the counterfeit of his best quality says it again. That reads as piling on.

The summary says 'Balanced: Little things, Others' wins, Follow-through', but the rails print Others' wins as 'Simply glad (33/100)' and Follow-through as 'Hard to finish (67/100)'. The report contradicts itself.
'Your gladness is a gift... the joy Christ promised' is thin for a man whose faith is 'there's probably something' and who prays when frightened.
Gluttony's closing advice about fasts and guests does not fit a man drinking cans after night shifts.
best_moment: 'It is not that you do not care. It is that the care arrives too late.' That, with the kindled-reeds anger reading and 'You would probably say you rarely hold a grudge. Ask someone close to you whether they agree', explains the shout-then-buy-a-can pattern back to him without scolding.
worst_moment: The report never tells him that people are afraid of him. That is the thing his friend and his eight-year-old both see, and he had half-said it himself with 'I don't always notice I've upset someone'. Instead it tells him three times that his anger dresses up as zeal.

type_why: 'Careful by nature, at your best when life is quiet' is Tomasz: he rechecks the signed-off calculations, walks the Tatras alone and stands by the window at name-day parties. 'You wait to be sure, and the moment can pass' is the bathroom that has been 'next spring' for six springs. The fear trap only half fits. Fear of running short is him. 'What if they are upset? What if I say it, and it costs me?' is not, because he barely minds what people think and simply goes on doing it his way.

links.link: Hard to start: people who never begin are busy with something else they love
links.why: This could have been sharp: the money he would rather keep is why the bathroom never starts. As written it is cryptic ('That has to be seen for what it is first').

links.link: Careful with what you have: tenacity is sometimes considered frugality
links.why: This is Beata's 'fight him for every zloty spent on anything enjoyable', set against his self-view of 'doesn't waste things'.

links.link: Keeps it in: more grievous loquacity in the heart; a door, not a wall
links.why: True of him, but the first link repeats it nearly word for word.

links.link: You listen more than you talk, and you have whole conversations in your head: an argument nobody can answer is easy to win
links.why: It explains his self-view exactly: open to other views, he simply finds most of them wrong. This is the report's real aha.

links.link: You let rudeness go, then hours later think of what you should have said
links.why: The text is identical to p01's. Nothing in his life or his wife's view suggests he replays slights. He leaves the room and carries on his own way.

links.link: You hold back after a hard day and notice when others overindulge: the pride of abstinence
links.why: His children's three streaming services, and the fight over every zloty spent on anything enjoyable.

links.link: You fix things and move on, but you're not one for saying sorry: a debtor is not absolved by borrowing no more
links.why: He shows love by fixing things, and is uneasy with feelings. 'Something still needs saying' is right.

links.link: Kindred: Nazianzen, Jeremiah, Arsenius
links.why: Arsenius sailing in silence fits the Tatras walker. Nazianzen, a poet and orator, sits oddly on an engineer who reads military history. Three kindred run together are a lot to take in.

fight_should_be: Greed, as given: 'the grip, not the amount... fear of having less... keeping a reserve and never feeling it is enough' is the emergency fund against his daughter's Netherlands plan. Listlessness second (his father, the bathroom) and pride third (rechecking everyone) are also right.
line_why: The Teacher is what he picked twice, so it is defensible. But the line his wife would name is the secret Giver: he slips his daughter money she doesn't know came from him and drives people to the airport at four in the morning. The report names the Giver only as 'Second' and says nothing about it.
leanings_wrong: Temper: the rail prints 'Fiery (33/100)' while the summary lists Temper as 'Balanced'. 'Fiery' is wrong for a man who leaves the room rather than raise his voice.
Mood: 'Heavy-hearted (71/100)'. He is serious and reserved, not heavy. Nobody around him describes low spirits, so the label overstates.
help_card_wrong: 'Argue it out with me. Win fairly and I will come round.' His wife calls him 'as reliable as a wall and just as hard to move'. His own answers say he holds firm (8/100) and usually goes ahead when friends think his plan is a mistake. The card repeats the self-image that the inner-talk link rightly punctures.

'Say "next time, try this", not "you did this wrong"' comes from his careful nerve. It sits against his explicit answers, 'Say it straight. I can take it' and 'Point out everything', and against line 7 of the same card.
wording_issues: The grip on money is named three times: the Careful-with-what-you-have leaning, the Greed fight and the Thrift counterfeit. The secret generosity his wife treasures ('generous in secret... kinder than he lets anyone see') is never credited. The 'generous in secret, stingy in public' aha was sitting in his answers (he picked 'Quietly pay for something they can't afford', and leans Better in private), and without it the report tips toward harsh.
The Keeps-it-in leaning and the first link say the same thing in nearly the same words: 'The talking does not stop. It moves inside, where nobody can answer'.

'A heart with no joy inside looks for comfort in owning things' is blunt, and not quite him (the allotment, the Tatras). It is Gregory's genealogy, but 'a heart that has lost its joy within' would be fairer.

Nazianzen: 'Near the end he said, "I am weary of being charged with my gentleness"'. The source is Oration 42, his farewell to Constantinople in 381, about nine years before he died. 'Near the end' is loose unless it says near the end of his time as bishop.
'Balanced: Others' wins, Temper' contradicts the rails, which print 'Simply glad (33/100)' and 'Fiery (33/100)'.
best_moment: 'An argument nobody can answer is easy to win. It can leave you quietly judging people who never got to reply.' That is precisely why a man who believes he is open to other views finds most of them wrong, and he had never put it that way.
worst_moment: Three separate warnings about holding on to money, and not one word for the father who slips his daughter money in secret. The Giver shows up only as a bare 'Second: The Giver', so the reading his wife would give ('kinder than he lets anyone see') is missing, and he comes out a miser.

type_why: The Herald fits how she sees herself and how Chioma sees her. She is first to volunteer, persuasive in a room and confident. The close call to The Spark fits the four notebooks and the forty chairs just as well. 'Restless mind (0/100)' and 'Hard to finish (92/100)' are dead right, and 'Finish one thing before you start the next' goes straight at her belief that her problem is too little time. The report still misses Chioma's central point: she is scared of stillness. The type line turns that into a strength ('at your best when there is something to do'). Self-report is not the excuse here. She answered k3 at full strength ('When you have nothing to do, your thoughts get worse. I'm better off busy'), k4 +3 ('a week at home with nothing to do' wears her out) and k1 -3. No sentence joins those answers to her busyness. 'Rest can feel like losing' and the Restlessness counterfeit come close but stop short. Chioma's other point is that she helps everybody so nobody gets close. Her answer se1 -2 ('People I've just met get the best of me') could have caught it, but it was blended into 'Seen and unseen: balanced'.

links.link: You said you tell people in charge when they are wrong. You also said your anger usually feels justified.
links.why: It is partly true, since she hates being told what to do and sighs at slow people. But it makes the same point as the 'Takes up room' bullet just above it (pride that thinks it is honesty). The paragraph is word for word what p05 got. 'Gregory would call that a pair' is still vague.

links.link: You said you let people know on the spot. You also said you snap, and wish you had not.
links.why: It fits her sharpness with slow people and the sighing out loud. 'The care arrives too late' is a good line. 'Gregory saw this exactly' overclaims a little.

fight_should_be: Listlessness, in Cassian's fleeing form, should lead or at least share the lead. It is ranked third here. Cassian's acedia cannot bear the cell. It hates the dull middle of the work and sends a person off to help others as 'a real work of piety'. That is Adaeze: the itch in the middle of every project, evenings filled so she is never alone, getting up to clean when the dread comes, helping everyone so nobody gets close. The acedia text in p06's report fits her better than it fits him. Pride is defensible now. The signs it lists (correction is hard to take, she prefers her own way) fit her own answers (y7 +2, mi2 +3) and her hating being told what to do. It is the right second.
line_why: The Teacher fits the free mentoring of secondary-school girls. The Giver as second fits sending fifty thousand naira to a stranger's hospital bill without checking.
best_moment: "Counterfeit: Restlessness. Not being able to stop can feel like faithfulness." This is the closest the report comes to Chioma's point that it isn't only ambition. 'Finish one thing before you start the next' is a close second, because it quietly answers her belief that time is the problem.
worst_moment: "3. Challenge me. I can handle it." This is on the card she would hand to other people. It contradicts the same report's Pride section ('Finding correction hard to take, even when it is fair'), her own private answer (y7 +2) and everything her friend and mother know: she hates being told what to do.
leanings_wrong: Correction: Say it straight (25/100). This rests on one mild public answer (c2 +1). Her private answer says correction is hard to take even when fair (y7 +2), and she hates being told what to do. The leaning shows the self-image, the report never sets the two side by side, and the help card then repeats the self-image.

Seen and unseen: balanced (42/100). She said clearly that people she has just met get the best of her (se1 -2). That is her friend's point that she is warm to strangers and mentees but nobody gets close. Blending it with se2 into 'balanced' buried the one answer that could have caught it.
help_card_wrong: "3. Challenge me. I can handle it." This contradicts the Pride section and her private answer that correction is hard to take even when fair.
"5. Be specific about what could be better." This is harmless but generic. The same line is on p05's card.
wording_issues: "Strongest leanings: Speaks up, Hard to finish, Takes up room" / "* Takes up room: You speak up to people in charge." The label still does not match its gloss, and 'Takes up room' in the headline reads as a jab.
"Whoever praises you can steer you." is followed at once by "What it costs you: Praise can steer you." This is still a straight repeat.
"Gregory would call that a pair." This is still vague, and the whole paragraph is identical to p05's.
"Right now: Pride. Last on Cassian's list, and first in its roots." This is still unclear to a reader who has not read Cassian. The sentences after it explain it better.

"(They picked: gladly do: Explain something until they finally understand it. / Quietly pay for something they can't afford.; people come for: ...)" This still reads like debug output: third person, with '.;' punctuation.

"Diligence: You keep working when others stop." It is true of her hours but reads as a contradiction of 'You start well, then fade' and 'Hard to finish (92/100)'. It flatters the self-image that the rest of the report corrects.

"And idle talk slides, step by step, into talk about other people." Nothing in her answers or her life points to gossip. It reads as a stock warning. 'Before you speak, ask whether it is needed, or kind' is mildly preachy.
"Close call: your second disposition is close". 'Second disposition' is unclear. The header uses 'disposition' for one axis only.
"Gregory saw this exactly." This overclaims.

type_why: The Deep Well fits: heavy-hearted, careful, quiet, holds firm. The trap ('a quarrel... It looks like being right about how badly you have been treated') is exactly what her sister sees with Maria and with the count of who came to Giorgos's memorials. 'Heaviness can turn into irritation' and 'Watch for bitterness that calls itself honesty' go straight at her self-view ('not harsh, only honest'). What self-report cannot see is her loneliness and her refusal to let anyone help. No question asks about accepting help, so that gap is fair. One of her strongest answers was a real chance, though. 'I stop doing it, but I'm not one for saying sorry' (af2 -3) is the pride her sister names. It became the pleasant-sounding leaning 'Moves on (83/100)'. 'People come to you when something really matters' is false of an isolated widow who distrusts anyone who tries to comfort her.

links.link: You said you hold back after a hard day. You also said you notice when other people overindulge.
links.why: 'Judging the undisciplined' brushes her 'young people are soft'. But her harshness comes from grief, not from food. This is the third time the same point and the same quote appear (the bullet, this link and the counterfeit).

links.link: You said you listen more than you talk. You also said you have whole conversations in your head that never happen.
links.why: This is the real aha of the report. She speaks little but judges much: cheerful people, Maria, who didn't come. 'An argument nobody can answer is easy to win' fits a woman who talks to her dead son more than to anyone living and keeps a silent tally.

links.link: You said you tell people in charge when they are wrong. You also said your anger usually feels justified.
links.why: For her, unlike p04, it lands. 'What feels like honesty can be pride' is her self-view exactly, and 'people in charge' covers her stubbornness with doctors. But the text is identical to p04's, and it repeats the Heavy-hearted counsel.

links.link: You said things stay with you for a while. You also said once you are angry, it can last for days.
links.why: A slow anger turning into a grudge fits the count of who came to the memorials. It is the third use of the 'moroseness easily slides into anger' quote, though.

fight_should_be: Sadness leading, as given, with Pride close behind. Sadness's own speech ('What ground hast thou to rejoice, when thou endurest so many wrongs from thy neighbours?') and 'The people you love come round, and everything they say seems badly timed' are nearly a portrait of her with Maria. Naming a loss as one of sadness's roots respects her grief without being told of it.
line_why: The Watcher fits the oil lamp before the icons, the daily cemetery lamp and the prayer rope held in the dark ('keep watch while others work'). The Giver as second fits the eggs and oil sent back twice over.
best_moment: "Where the trap is set for you: a quarrel... It looks like being right about how badly you have been treated." This names what her sister sees without accusing her. It is matched by the Sadness section's "What takes its place: Not cheerfulness." That line respects her contempt for cheerful people and her grief at the same time.
worst_moment: "How you speak: Full in both. You think things through, and the words come easily. Gregory calls this speaker 'worthy of praise'. The gift is meant to be used for others." She speaks little, and the few words she does say cut Maria. The text is still identical to p06's, and it praises the very thing that wounds her family.
leanings_wrong: After a mistake: Moves on (83/100). This is built mostly on 'I stop doing it, but I'm not one for saying sorry' (af2 -3). For a woman who never apologises to Maria and keeps grudges, 'Moves on' reads as the opposite of the truth. That answer was the pride her sister names, and the report turned it into a compliment.

Seen and unseen: balanced (58/100). She said people she has just met get the best of her (se1 -1). Her sister says she is cruel to the one closest, Maria, while neighbours get eggs and oil. Blending it into 'balanced' lost that.
help_card_wrong: "5. Say 'next time, try this', not 'you did this wrong'." This contradicts her own 'Say it straight. I can take it' (c2 +3) and the report's 'Correction: Say it straight (8/100)'. She would call this soft.
"3. Ask what I think. I rarely offer it." She does offer it, unasked and cuttingly ('the lentils are too salty'). This clashes with the report's 'Says it plainly' and 'Lets them know' leanings.
"1. Show me. Let me see someone do it." This is harmless but generic for a 74-year-old deciding whether to leave her house.
wording_issues: "You feel things deeply and think them through. People come to you when something really matters." The second sentence is still generic, and false of her.
"the pride of abstinence" is still quoted three times in one report: the Keeps a tight rein bullet, the first link and the counterfeit.
"moroseness easily slides into anger" is also quoted three times: the trap, the Heavy-hearted bullet and the fourth link.

"He opens his Dialogues alone in a place he says suited "a sad and melancholy disposition", and he wrote that he loved the quiet life and had the busy one forced on him." This is still one long comma-joined sentence.

"Your seriousness is not a flaw to be fixed. Held under reason, the fire in it becomes holy zeal." The quote is about anger, not seriousness. The jump from 'seriousness' to 'the fire in it' is not explained.

"Quick and lasting. Your anger catches fast" She answered 'Slowly. It takes a lot' (an1 +1). The lasting half is right, but she will read the first half as wrong. "It is also the one where a little work changes the most." is unsourced, and it sits right after Gregory's words, so it reads as his.
"Your strength: Counsel. Its partner: Courage. ... The risk is that you never get round to doing it." This is still identical to p06's.
"(They picked: gladly do: Pray for them every day, without telling them. / Have them over and cook them a meal.; people come for: Money, or something they need.)" This still reads like debug output.

Tone: for a mother two years after her son's death, anger or judging is named in the trap, two bullets, three of the four links, the anger section ('he calls this the worst') and the fight. Only the Sadness section acknowledges a loss. Each point is fair to what her sister sees, but together they can read as a scolding. The overlap between the trap, the Heavy-hearted bullet and links 3 and 4 could be cut.

type_why: The strongest leanings are the friend's view, not the self-image: Lets it go (100), Keeps the peace (100), Easily swayed (100), Chooses what to show (75). That is Kayla's 'no spine' and 'never sure what he really thinks'. But The Hearth's headline and blurb are Jake's own mask: 'Your mood runs light... You enjoy things as they come... People tend to relax around you... You think best in quiet.' His answers held the stress Kayla sees, and the report never joins it up: Careful (79), 'What if I can't?' (+2), 'One raised eyebrow can stay with me all day' (+2), 'The fear of letting people down', criticism stays longer, and privately 'I put off the one thing that matters most' (+3) and 'I can't settle' (+2). The close call, The Still Water, is nearer the real Jake. 'Chooses what to show (75)' is his chameleon side, and no sentence uses it.

links.link: You said you let rudeness go. You also said hours later you think of what you should have said.
links.why: It rests on a strong answer (w2 -3), and 'The hard part for you is not staying calm. It is the evening after' is well put. It never reaches the point that his evenings go to games, and it contradicts the anger section's 'it does not last'.

links.link: You said you let things slide that you probably should not. You also said you calm things down when friends argue.
links.why: 'Keeping the peace can be love. It can also be the easier road' is Kayla's view and the 'haha yeah' texts. It repeats the Keeps the peace bullet, though, and the Sloth quote appears again in the counterfeit.

links.link: You said you let small things slide. You also said your worst mistakes are small, but they add up.
links.why: It fits the few minutes late every shift, routines that last nine days, 'tomorrow I'll go to bed at a normal time' and $4,000 of loans already. 'No drop matters until the river floods' lands.

fight_should_be: Listlessness, as given. 'Checking your phone again. Putting off the thing that matters' is his nights and his unmade program choice. 'Courage' as its replacement, and 'work with your hands, and stay put', speak straight to the choice he is avoiding. The pious-excuse half ('a real work of piety') fits p04 better than him. 'Cassian says sadness feeds it' could have named Cassian's anxious kind of sadness, which is Jake's.
line_why: The Caregiver fits picking up his half-sister without complaint and his patience with old men hunting for the right bolt. The Teacher as second is plausible.
best_moment: "Gregory says the changeable do not trust their own judgment, because they think too little of themselves... Counsel: Trust your judgment a little more. It is better than you think." This turns his 'open-minded' self-image into the truth Kayla sees, and it says it kindly. It bears directly on the choice he hasn't told his mother or his friend about.
worst_moment: The type's opening: "Your mood runs light, and you are at your best when life is quiet. You enjoy things as they come: a meal, a long talk, an evening at home. People tend to relax around you." It confirms the chill mask he hides behind. His own answers showed the stress under the jokes, and his evenings go to games until three or four, not long talks.
leanings_wrong: Make-up: Quiet mind (83/100). This is his self-image. Kayla says he games so he doesn't have to think, and his private answers ('I can't settle to what I'm meant to be doing' +2, 'I put off the one thing that matters most' +3) sit against 'your thoughts settle'. 'You think best in quiet' follows from it.

Mood: Light-hearted (21/100). His mood answers were light, so this is a limit of self-report, not a scoring error. But the report never sets it against his Careful 79 and 'What if I can't?', which is where Kayla's 'far more stressed than he acts' shows.
help_card_wrong: "6. Argue it out with me. Win fairly and I will come round." This invites the exact dynamic Kayla names (he agrees with whoever talked last). It fights the report's own counsel to trust his judgment more, and he hates conflict.
The card has seven items where the others have five. It is long, and it mixes gentle ('A hint is enough') with 'Argue it out'.
wording_issues: "Later they remember it, and start looking for ways to get even." This is still unfair to Jake, who shows no vengefulness. The link below it says it better ('wishing you had been harsher than you would ever actually be').
"Counsel: Guard your heart after the win." It is still unclear what 'the win' is.
"Slow and brief... it does not last" contradicts the report's own link ('on a quiet evening, it comes back bigger than it was') and bullet ('Later they remember it').

"Keep it that way. When someone wrongs you, remember your own faults first." This is the wrong medicine for a conflict-avoider whom the report elsewhere says 'thinks too little of himself'. It pushes him further into swallowing things.
"Sloth is frequently looked upon as a maintenance of peace" is still quoted twice (link 2 and the counterfeit).

"How you speak: Full in both... Gregory calls this speaker 'worthy of praise'. The gift is meant to be used for others." This is still identical to p05's. It praises the speech of a man who texts 'haha yeah' to things he disagrees with and rarely says what he wants.

"Your strength: Counsel... You think it through well." This is identical to p05's and flatters someone who finds both the apologetics and the atheist clips convincing. 'The risk is that you never get round to doing it' does fit.

"Your gladness is a gift. Kept close to God, it becomes the joy Christ promised... (Christ, quoted by Gregory in the Pastoral Rule)" In Pastoral Rule III.2, Gregory sets John 16:22 before the SAD and 'Woe unto you that laugh now' before the joyful. Using it to bless a light-hearted type reverses Gregory's own use. It is not invented, but it is misapplied. It also speaks to the mask, not the anxious young man under it.

"When he came out, Athanasius says, his friends were amazed at how settled he was, and his face was cheerful because his soul was at peace." This merges two scenes in Athanasius (the friends' amazement after twenty years, and the cheerful face from the joy of his soul later in the Life) into one comma-joined sentence. As a kindred for Jake, Antony is generic to the type.
"(They picked: gladly do: Sit with them at the hospital, or through a bad night. / Explain something until they finally understand it.; people come for: ...)" This still reads like debug output.

type_why: The restless make-up is right. She sleeps five hours, cannot bear an empty weekend and is weighing a job with even longer hours, so 'Rest can feel like losing' lands. The light-hearted disposition is wrong. Her mood came out 42/100, a coin flip the report itself calls a 'close call'. That coin flip drives four sections: the pleasure trap, the young Augustine as kindred, 'You make hard things feel lighter' and 'Your gladness is a gift'. None of them fits a woman whose own bars say she keeps a tight rein on comforts. 'People relax around you' is true of the ward and false at home, where the children tiptoe. Her truer disposition is confident and in charge.

links.link: Lets them know + snaps and wishes she had not -> 'the care arrives too late'
links.why: This is her evening at home exactly. She knows it, it bothers her at night, and it happens again the next day.

links.link: Tells people in charge + anger feels justified -> 'the feeling of being right is not proof'
links.why: It goes straight at her self-view: firm because someone has to be, and sure she is fair to everyone.

links.link: Takes a stand -> quarrels grow from pride in a gift that sets us apart, like knowing more or trying harder
links.why: She is the senior nurse who carries everything and will not be second-guessed, least of all by Peter.

links.link: Kindled reeds: flares and fades, plus 'Ask someone close to you whether they agree'
links.why: The hedge points her toward Wanjiru's view without accusing her.

links.link: Trap = pleasure ('one more helping, one more episode')
links.why: Her own leanings say she keeps a tight rein on comforts and is careful with what she has. Her trap is control and temper, not indulgence.

links.link: Kindred: Augustine as a young man, loving talk, jokes and pleasure
links.why: A 45-year-old ward sister who dozes through the sermon from exhaustion is not the pleasure-loving young Augustine.

fight_should_be: Pride first is right: she prefers her own way and will not let Peter carry anything. Anger should be second. Her nightly flare at home is her most visible fault, but the only private anger item asks about replaying wrongs, so a quick temper ranks below Greed. Greed should sit lower, or be explained as fear about school fees. She gives freely to every funeral collection.
line_why: Caregiver: she holds a frightened teenager's hand at three in the morning, and this is her life's work. Giver as second fits the collections. But it only reflects her own picks back to her, so there is no discovery here.
leanings_wrong: Seen and unseen: balanced (50/100). She answered that people she has just met get the best of her, and her sister calls her a saint to strangers and a sergeant to her family. That is her defining split. It was caught by one question and then cancelled out by a second question that measures something else ('I don't much mind what people think'), so it ends up filed under 'Balanced' with no comment.
Mood: the headline says 'Light-hearted' and 'Cheerful by disposition', but the Mood bar right below says balanced (42/100). The page contradicts itself.
Correction: Say it straight (33/100). That is her self-image. In private she admitted that correction is hard to take, and her sister says she hates being second-guessed.
wording_issues: Anger-as-righteousness comes up three times. The same Gregory line, 'they think the goad of their anger to be the zeal of righteousness', is printed twice (the Fiery bullet and 'What you might not have noticed' #2), and the counterfeit says it again in other words. Anger appears in six sections in all. It starts to read as a lecture.

'Full in both. You think things through...' contradicts her own answer that she sometimes speaks before she has thought it through. Calling her a speaker 'worthy of praise' flatters words her family experiences as orders.
'Greed' is shown second of eight with no explanation. That will sting a woman whose tightness is fear about fees and who gives freely elsewhere.
'Your gladness is a gift' is generic. It rests on the coin-flip mood axis.
'Last on Cassian's list, and first in its roots' is insider phrasing and hard to parse.
best_moment: 'It is not that you do not care. It is that the care arrives too late.' This is paired with her answers that she lets people know on the spot and snaps and wishes she had not. It names the thing that keeps her awake at night without making her a villain.
worst_moment: 'Where the trap is set for you: pleasure... one more helping, one more episode.' She sleeps five hours, and her own bar says she keeps a tight rein on comforts. Meanwhile the one answer that matched her sister's verdict, that strangers get the best of her, is filed under 'Balanced' and never mentioned.

type_why: 'The Lookout', careful and restless, is Daniel: checking the gas, worrying in loops, tense on holiday, unable to nap. 'Worry can pass for wisdom' answers his self-view ('my worrying is just good sense') head on. Two parts lean toward a timid man, when he is an over-doer: 'You wait to be sure, and the moment can pass', and the reluctant Moses and Gideon as kindred. The trap's example worries ('What if they are upset? What if I say it, and it costs me?') are about social nerves. His real worries are the mortgage, promotion and his son's school.

links.link: Listens more than talks + whole conversations in his head -> 'an argument nobody can answer is easy to win... quietly judging people who never got to reply'
links.why: This is the closest the report gets to Soo-jin's view. He trusts no one to do it right. He rewrites his team's reports at night instead of telling them, and he goes cold and precise instead of arguing out loud.

links.link: Keeps disagreements with superiors to himself + never good enough -> fear passing as humility
links.why: It fits his politeness to superiors and his fear of being passed over. It is not his main blind spot, which is control called responsibility.

links.link: Prudence, counterfeit: fear calling itself caution
links.why: This is the exact rebuttal of his self-view.

links.link: Chooses what to show -> 'Let one person see all of you'
links.why: He laughs alone in the dark at old shows and only then feels like himself. His wife says he is never really in the room.

links.link: Hard on yourself -> Gregory's faint-hearted, who sink into discouragement
links.why: Daniel is not discouraged. He is driven. He never feels finished, and he pushes harder.

links.link: Heavy-hearted -> 'bitterness that calls itself honesty'
links.why: His coldness could fit this, but the line is loose and he would not recognise it.

links.link: Kindred: Moses begging God to send someone else; Gideon obeying at night
links.why: Both are about shrinking from a call. Daniel does the opposite: he takes on everything and delegates nothing.

links.link: Counsel as the partner of courage: 'The risk is that you never get round to doing it'
links.why: He pays before anyone asks and rewrites reports at midnight. His risk is never letting anyone else do it.

fight_should_be: Pride first is right, and his private answer that he would do most things better than the people around him supports it. But the copy is generic, word for word the same as another person's report, and never says what his wife says: that he calls it responsibility but it is control. Listlessness (restless, there and not there, checking email at red lights) belongs above Greed. Greed at third is doubtful for a man who pays before anyone asks. His fear is about the mortgage, not a love of money.
line_why: Giver fits: he is generous with his parents and pays for things before anyone asks. Teacher as second fits a father who re-checks homework the tutor has already checked. The report never squares this with its own bar 'Having: Careful with what you have (83)'.
leanings_wrong: Temper: Fiery (25/100). He rarely gets loud and goes cold and precise. The report's own anger section says 'It takes a lot to make you angry'. The label comes from indignation items and misleads.
When wronged: Lets it go (75/100). He goes cold, his anger lasts days, and the report's own 'once it is lit, it stays lit' contradicts it.
Pace: Puts it off (75/100). He over-does and over-checks. Only his big decisions (the academies, Vietnam) are slow.
Room: Makes yourself small (75/100). This half fits: he is polite to superiors but is a deacon and a quietly demanding manager.
help_card_wrong: 'Say next time, try this, not you did this wrong' and 'Start with what I did well' go against his own answers. He said 'Say it straight. I can take it', 'Point out everything. I'd rather know', and that praise feels like people just being kind.
The card leaves out 'Tell me plainly what to do', which he chose.
wording_issues: The Temper bar reads 'Fiery' beside 'Hard wood... it takes a lot to make you angry', and 'When wronged: Lets it go' sits beside 'it stays lit'. The page contradicts itself.
The Pride block is the same template text another person got. Nothing in it is tied to his answers.
'Having: Careful with what you have' and 'The Giver... Money, time, things' sit side by side with no word on how both are true: generous with his parents, frightened by the mortgage.
The trap's example worries are generic social-nerves lines, not his.
'Last on Cassian's list, and first in its roots' is insider phrasing.
best_moment: 'Worry can pass for wisdom', echoed later by 'Fear can call itself caution'. It answers his belief that his worrying is just good sense. Close behind: 'It can leave you quietly judging people who never got to reply.'
worst_moment: 'You think it through well. The risk is that you never get round to doing it', along with 'Pace: Puts it off'. This is said to a man who rewrites his team's reports at midnight rather than send them back. His real risk is the reverse.

type_why: 'The Spark' is Fe: she fills a room, plays pagode loud, and comes alive when busy. 'You can skip past what is wrong' quietly touches the hidden card statements. The pleasure trap is right in kind, but its examples ('one more helping, one more episode') miss her actual form of it. She buys things to feel better and to be liked.

links.link: Lets them know + snaps and wishes she had not -> 'the care arrives too late'
links.why: She flares at rude clients, says something she cannot take back, and stews for a day. Her friend says her temper has driven off good clients.

links.link: Tells people in charge + anger feels justified -> 'the feeling of being right is not proof'
links.why: It is true enough, but it is a second anger point after the first, and word for word the same as another person's. Her answers set up a money link instead, and that went unused.

links.link: Speaks up -> much talk scatters the mind and slides into talk about other people
links.why: She knows every client's love life. 'No power to turn back within' also fits her crying for ten minutes and then scrolling.

links.link: Open-handed -> giving so much at once that you run short
links.why: The Christmas she could not afford, and the dinners she pays for 'because I owe them'.

links.link: Generosity, counterfeit: 'prodigality hides itself under the appellation of liberality'
links.why: This is the one place the report reaches her friend's verdict that she is a disaster with money.

links.link: Kindred: Augustine as a young man, who loved talk, jokes and friends
links.why: It is a fair match for her warmth and her crowd of friends, and not unkind.

links.link: Troubles you least: Greed
links.why: It is correct in Cassian's sense, since she hoards nothing. But unexplained, it tells a woman who hides R$18,000 of statements in a drawer and blames bad luck that money is not her problem.

fight_should_be: Anger and Gluttony as co-leads is fair. But her largest fault, as her friend sees it, is spending to feel better and to be liked, and that falls between Cassian's labels and is never named. Sadness (crying on the back step) belongs above seventh, though self-report hid most of it. Vainglory (spending to be liked) belongs above sixth. The Anger detail 'Going cold on people while saying you are fine' does not fit her hot, open temper.
line_why: Caregiver: she sits with her mother at the clinic for hours without complaint. Host as second: the dinners for her girlfriends.
leanings_wrong: Mood: Light-hearted (13/100). This is true of the salon, but she cries alone on the back step. Self-report could not see that, and the report never hints at a low under the cheer.
wording_issues: Both 'What you might not have noticed' paragraphs are word for word the same as p07's, and both are about anger again. Her answers set up the aha her friend names: give on impulse and regret it, treat yourself, 'small ones, but they add up', and privately 'I put off the one thing that matters most'. The link could have been drawn and was not.
'It is also the one where a little work changes the most' follows 'Gregory did not soften it', so it reads as Gregory's claim. It is unsourced.
'The fix is simple: think first.' is glib.
The Open-handed counsel 'do not keep score' does not match her problem. She gives to be liked and cannot afford it.
Tone risk: she is a seeker who already feels judged at church. Talking too much, the worst kind of anger, the pleasure trap and prodigality stack up, with little said to the sadness under the cheer.
best_moment: 'Scattering can call itself generosity. "prodigality hides itself under the appellation of liberality"', with the Open-handed warning about running short. It names her generosity and her debt as one thing, without scolding.
worst_moment: 'Troubles you least: Greed' closes her private fight with no gloss. Neither 'noticed' paragraph touches money. So the report never says what her friend says she most needs to hear: that she spends to feel better and must look at the numbers. The questions did catch it.

type_why: 'At your best when there is something to do' is Bob: the oatmeal at six, the widow's lawn, the garage. But the fear trap ('What if they are upset? What if I say it, and it costs me?') is not him. He is steady, not a worrier. By Mike's account his trap is pride: he will not let anyone help, and he is wearing out. 'Restless by make-up' is the wrong word for a steady man. It is also awkward that 'Your opposite: The Oak' names the word anyone who knows Bob would use for him: rooted, 54 years married, in the same pew since 1971. Moses fits: slow of speech, and forty years of carrying people. Gideon, frightened and working at night, does not.

links.link: Conversations in your head plus listening more than talking, read as quietly judging people who never got to reply ('his mind he exalts')
links.why: Bob is not a silent judge of others. What he keeps behind the wall is his own need: that he is drowning and needs help. The link finds the right wall but the wrong thing behind it. It also repeats the Keeps-it-in card almost word for word.

links.link: Fixes things and moves on, but is not one for saying sorry, so the debt is not yet paid
links.why: It matches the garage. He bangs around, comes back and answers June gently, and never names it. 'Something still needs saying' is a fair, small nudge. It also applies to his children, whom he is holding off.

fight_should_be: Pride of the self-sufficient kind: he helps everyone and will not be helped, whether with the knee, the aide or video calls. Sadness should come close behind (the weariness, the blue evenings with westerns). Listlessness belongs only as a symptom of the decisions he puts off.
line_why: The Caregiver: 'You sit with people, and you do not leave.' That is Bob with June, exactly. The Giver second (tips well, buys the Girl Scout cookies) is also right.
leanings_wrong: Make-up: Restless mind (33): he is steady, and 'at your best with something to do' is right while 'restless' is not
Nerve: Careful (67): the score may be fair, but the type text reads it as fear and worry, which is not Bob
Correction: Say it straight (8): it is then glossed through Gregory's chapter on the impudent ('the bold'). Liking plain feedback is not impudence.
wording_issues: The top three lines say the same thing three times: 'Careful by nature, and at your best when...', then 'Careful by disposition. Restless by make-up.', then 'You are careful by nature, and you are at your best with something to do.'
'The talking does not stop. It moves inside, where nobody can answer it' appears in the Keeps-it-in card and again, nearly verbatim, in the first link.
'Your strength: Counsel... The risk is that you never get round to doing it' repeats the Deliberation/Delay counterfeit just above it. The block is identical in all three reports.
'Gregory says the bold often do not see they are in the wrong': Gregory's word is 'the impudent'. Softening it hides that the mapping is a stretch.
The Listlessness signs ('Checking your phone again', 'Watching the clock') are generic. This is a man who will not learn video calls.
The 'people come for:' field trails off empty in the picks line.
'Your care is a gift. Gregory says the fearful should not stay in fear' is a fixed block, identical across all three reports.
best_moment: Three lines together describe his standoff with his daughter over the aide and the knee: 'Deliberation... Counterfeit: Delay. Putting off can pass for thinking it through.' Then the Holds-firm counsel, 'Take good advice, even when it was not your idea.' Then the help card, 'Give me time to come round. Pressure makes me dig in.' His kids would recognise all three.
worst_moment: It names Listlessness as his main fight, shown as clock-watching and phone-checking and cured by 'work with your hands, and stay put'. This is a man who is up at six making June's oatmeal and has stayed put for 54 years. The report never touches what Mike sees: too proud to admit he is drowning. 'Ask for my help. I will give it gladly' holds half the truth and misses the other half: he will not ask. Self-report partly explains this, because Bob calls himself a regular guy. But no item asks whether he finds it harder to give help or to accept it, and that item would have caught it.

type_why: The Still Water says she is 'at your best when life is quiet' and 'You think best in quiet'. It pairs her with Gregory Nazianzen ('weary of being charged with my gentleness'), Arsenius sailing in silence, and Jeremiah too young to speak. She is a sharp, talkative, fiery English teacher. The fear trap ('What if I say it, and it costs me?') contradicts her own top leanings, printed a few lines below: Takes a stand (0), Fiery (8), Lets them know (17). Her 'Careful' score measures pessimism (she expects the worst and says so), not timidity, but the type text reads it as timidity. One line lands: 'Worry can pass for wisdom.' That is her cynicism passing for realism, and it deserved to be the headline. She will judge the whole report by the header, and she is exactly the reader who screenshots it.

links.link: Lets people know on the spot, and snaps and wishes she had not, so 'the care arrives too late'
links.why: It is her mother: impatient on the phone, then over with the shopping for three hours. This is the one genuine aha in the report.

links.link: Tells people in charge they are wrong, and her anger usually feels justified, so 'the feeling of being right is not proof'
links.why: It is fair and balanced ('Neither means you are wrong'). But it is the third time the report says her anger may be pride. Aoife says she is more hurt by the Church than angry with it, so a third warning about righteous-feeling anger will read to her as a lecture.

fight_should_be: Sadness should lead: the hidden hurt and tiredness Aoife sees, over the Church and her mother, with Anger as its outward form. The nightly wine is how that shows, so Gluttony as a close second is fair. But the report should say what she is taking the edge off.
line_why: The Advocate with The Teacher fits well: the housing arguments, and tearing an essay apart then lending the kid a life-changing book. Teacher could reasonably lead.
leanings_wrong: Make-up: Quiet mind (63): she reads the news too much and lies awake replaying online arguments. This is partly her own answers, but the label is wrong for her.

Candour: Says it plainly (25): she says plenty about the world and almost nothing about herself, which is the armour Aoife names. The forced A/B pair could not separate saying what you think from showing what you feel.
wording_issues: The fixed disposition blocks contradict her leanings: the fear trap, 'Your care is a gift. Gregory says the fearful should not stay in fear', and 'Your strength: Counsel... The risk is that you never get round to doing it' (she rushes in).
The same Gregory line ('they think the goad of their anger to be the zeal of righteousness') is quoted twice. The Zeal counterfeit then says it a third time. That makes it preachy by repetition.
'Gregory did not soften it: of the four, he calls this the worst.' This is harsh in a first read, even though the next sentence softens it.
Gluttony's 'own speech' is about eating ('all things clean, in order to be eaten'). Her pull is wine, so the quote sits oddly.
Arsenius is described as 'sailing in silence'. The source says 'in perfect peace', a small drift in a saint's story.
best_moment: 'It is not that you do not care. It is that the care arrives too late.' This is the phone call with her mother followed by three hours with the shopping.
worst_moment: The first screen: 'The Still Water... at your best when life is quiet', with Arsenius and Nazianzen's gentleness, sits above leanings headed Takes a stand, Fiery, Lets them know. After that the report never sees what Aoife sees: the cynicism is armour, and she is hurt more than angry and softer than anyone in the room. That was within reach of her own answers. Heavy-hearted (75) next to Fiery (8), plus choosing 'angry' over 'low' after a bad day, could have supported 'when you are hurt, it comes out sharp, not sad.' Instead the report reads her anger as the root three times over.

type_why: The type is careful and quiet, and 'A crowded week wears you down faster than it does most' suits a man driving fifty hours with three noisy roommates. The fear trap ('What if I say it, and it costs me?') is the roommates and the young woman at church, exactly. Arsenius (a monk of the desert tradition his church honours) rings true for the creek-trail walks with church songs. So does Jeremiah, too young to speak, for a man who does not know how to begin.

links.link: Conversations in his head plus listening, read as quietly judging people who never got to reply
links.why: He silently stews over the roommates' noise and mess and never tells them. The only flaw is that it repeats the Keeps-it-in card almost word for word.

links.link: Lets rudeness go, and hours later thinks of what he should have said, so 'the hard part is the evening after'
links.why: It catches what Yonas sees and Samuel does not: he is less patient than he thinks. The irritation piles up until he leaves for his cousin's for the weekend.

links.link: Keeps disagreements with people in charge to himself, and never thinks his work good enough, so some of what feels like humility may be fear
links.why: This is the best line in the report. It speaks to the young woman at church, the roommates and the failed exam without naming any of them.

links.link: Holds back after a hard day, and notices when others overindulge, so 'the pride of abstinence'
links.why: He finds the bar crowds degrading, and other drivers call him stubborn. It is sharp but fair, and framed kindly ('Discipline is a gift').

fight_should_be: Sadness should lead: the loneliness he calls busyness, and what Yonas describes as never letting himself enjoy anything. Anger held in (the piled-up irritation) should come second. Greed should not be here. His grip on money is duty to his mother and sisters, not grasping.
line_why: The Giver fits: he sends $600 a month home. The Watcher second fits a man who fasts and prays. The report misses the obvious aha, though: the Giver who cannot give to himself.
leanings_wrong: Having: Careful with what you have (83): true as thrift, but the report turns it into the Greed verdict. His carefulness is for others.
Pace: Puts it off (92): overstated for a man who works fifty hours and studies at night. He is slow to decide, then firm, which is not the same as putting things off.
wording_issues: 'Guard your heart after the win': 'the win' is never explained. It is Gregory's victory of patience, and it is opaque in plain English.
'start looking for ways to get even' overstates Samuel. He withdraws; he does not retaliate.
The idea 'calm now, vexed later' is told three times: the Lets-it-go card, the second link, and Hard wood.
The Keeps-the-peace card and the Peace/Avoidance counterfeit make the same point twice.
The Greed signs ('Keeping a reserve, and never feeling it is enough') misread a reserve that is really his family's.
The help card has seven items where the others have four, so it reads as a list rather than a portrait.
Arsenius is described as 'sailing in silence'. The source says 'in perfect peace'.
best_moment: 'Some of what feels like humility may be fear of how it will land.' Together with 'The hard part for you is not staying calm. It is the evening after.' This is the aha Yonas would recognise: he believes he is more patient than he is.
worst_moment: 'Right now: Greed.' It tells him 'a heart with no joy inside looks for comfort in owning things' and 'cut the desire, not only the spending. Be content with what you need.' He owns two pairs of shoes, eats lentils all week, sends $600 home and feels guilty buying anything for himself. It contradicts the report's own Giver line, and it could deepen the joyless self-denial his cousin worries about. The private item ('hard to let go of money... even small amounts') cannot tell thrift-for-others from grip. But his Giver picks were right there to cross-check. Meanwhile the word 'lonely' never appears, though Heavy-hearted 79, Keeps it in 100, Makes yourself small 92 and Keeps a tight rein 92 all point straight at it.

type_why: The Careful half is exactly her. 'Your temptation... looks like worry. What if they are upset?... What if I say it, and it costs me?' is Chloe. The Quiet half and the name 'The Still Water' do not fit a woman whose mind never stops: she rewrites texts five times, reads chest twinges as heart trouble, and says her thoughts get worse when she is idle. Her make-up scored 58, which is balanced. Yet the header still prints 'Quiet by make-up'. The close-call note (The Lookout) is honest and should carry more weight. The kindred are mixed. Jeremiah's 'too young to speak' fits a frightened 23-year-old. Nazianzen's 'keep free from business' does not fit someone who takes every extra shift because she cannot say no, though 'weary of being charged with my gentleness' does land for a lovely doormat.

links.link: Lets rudeness go / hours later thinks of what she should have said
links.why: This is the silent fuming over the housemates' dishes. 'You can end up wishing you had been harsher than you would ever actually be' is kind and accurate. So is 'the hard part is the evening after'.

links.link: A mistake stays with her / quick to say sorry, and sometimes does it again
links.why: Her 'sorry' is a reflex; she apologises to furniture. It is not repentance for a sin she keeps committing. Using the image of washing and walking back into the mud, and saying 'feeling bad cannot do the work of changing', gives a scrupulous person more false guilt. Her friend's view is the reverse: she thinks she is selfish far more often than she is. Her answers already showed this pattern: 'not good enough', 'they're just being kind', 'feel bad for a long time'. The questions could have caught it.

links.link: Listens more than talks / whole conversations in her head
links.why: It is half right. Her silent anger at housemates really is 'judging people who never got to reply'. But most of her inner talk is anxious rehearsal and self-accusation, not winning arguments. The quote 'his mind he exalts' points to pride, which the same report ranks as the fault that troubles her least. This paragraph is word for word the same as p14's.

links.link: Keeps disagreements with people in charge to herself / never thinks her work is good enough
links.why: This is the best line in the report. It names why she cannot tell a doctor he has got something wrong, and it questions her self-image: 'Some of what feels like humility may be fear of how it will land.' It is new to her and it matters for a nurse.

fight_should_be: Anger or sadness. Anger is the silent fuming she then feels guilty for; her replay answer caught it. Sadness is the grief since her friend's death, plus 'most things stay with me'. Her putting-off is mostly fear of choosing (Christmas, going back to church). The type section already names that fear as her trap, so calling it listlessness diagnoses the same behaviour twice under two names. 'Watching the clock, checking your phone' is stock text, not her. 'Work with your hands' is odd advice for someone doing 20+ hours a week on top of final-year placement.
line_why: She is a nursing student who notices when a patient is scared, and people tell her things they tell no one else. 'You sit with people, and you do not leave' is her. It is the warmest true thing in the report.
leanings_wrong: Make-up is shown as balanced (58/100), but the header says 'Quiet by make-up'.

The 'Better in public' label (Seen and unseen, 17/100) reads like a charge of being two-faced. What her answers actually said is that she is at her best with new people and cares too much what people think. At home she is the same gentle person who washes everyone's dishes.

The 'Lets it go' note says the patient 'start looking for ways to get even'. That is true to Gregory but too strong for her. Link 1 later says the same thing better, from the same passage, so the point is made twice.
wording_issues: 'Guard your heart after the win.' is opaque where it appears. 'The win' is only explained two sections later.
The type is said three times in a row: the subtitle, 'Careful by disposition. Quiet by make-up.', and the first sentence of Your type. 'A crowded week wears you down' also appears twice.
'Those are the same thing.' (link 3) is a glib jump.
The counterfeit quote 'Sloth is frequently looked upon as a maintenance of peace' is aimed at a woman who works every shift she is offered. The word 'sloth' will read as one more accusation.
The anger cure 'think about your own faults too' feeds a person who already thinks about little else. So does link 2.
Nothing in the report says what her friend sees: that she is much stronger than she thinks. The partner virtue 'Courage' and 'love does what fear used to do' come close, but never say it to her.
best_moment: 'You said you keep your disagreements with people in charge to yourself. You also said you never think your work is good enough... Some of what feels like humility may be fear of how it will land.' Together with 'your temptation rarely looks like temptation. It looks like worry', this names her real pattern in a way she has not put into words.
worst_moment: The 'wash, and then walk straight back into the mud' link. It reads her reflexive apologising as unrepented sin and tells her that feeling bad 'cannot do the work of changing'. For a scrupulous seeker who already thinks she is selfish far more often than she is, this adds guilt where her friend would remove it.

type_why: Serious and restless both fit: he is better busy, idle time is worse, and he half waits for the catch. The trap does not fit as written. 'It looks like being right about how badly you have been treated' describes a grievance-holder, and Viktor never complains about his own pain or his lower pay. He grumbles about politicians, prices and young people, and takes his heaviness for realism. The truer trap, which his answers could show (half waits for the catch, thinks of what could go wrong), is gloom passing for realism. The kindred are two famous talkers, Chrysostom the preacher and Jerome the letter-writer. That is a poor match for a man his wife calls a closed door, though Chrysostom dying in exile has a quiet echo the report does not use.

links.link: Listens more than talks / whole conversations in his head
links.why: This is the same paragraph Chloe got, word for word. His fixed verdicts on people give 'quietly judging' some grip. But what he holds in is fear for Andriy and the talk about going home, not arguments he is winning. The report spends his 'keeps it in' material on judging instead of on carrying things alone.

links.link: Fixes it and moves on / stops doing wrong but is not one for saying sorry
links.why: This is the one real aha. He quit drinking alone, with shaking hands, and told nobody. 'Stopping is good... Something still needs saying' points straight at the apology Halyna never got. The report cannot know about the drinking, and still lands on it.

links.link: Things stay with him / anger lasts for days
links.why: On days with no message from Andriy he is gruff and silent until evening. Once he decides someone is not serious, he never changes his mind. 'A heavy heart slides into anger' fits. But it repeats the same Moralia quote used in the type section.

links.link: Careful about small things / worst mistakes rare but big
links.why: This is true of many careful tradesmen. Nothing ties it to him beyond the two answers, and 'the feeling of safety is where the big fall comes from' does not point at anything in his life.

fight_should_be: Sadness first: the dread about Andriy at the front, the half hour in the parked car, and a heaviness he calls realism. Anger comes close behind. Pride, in the form of his stubborn streak and his refusal to learn Polish, is real but second. The report says Pride and Sadness are close, which is honest. But it then describes only Pride, and sadness is the fight his wife would name. Also, 'What feeds it: vainglory' sits beside 'Troubles you least: Vainglory' with no word to reconcile them.
line_why: He fixed a neighbour's mother's car for nothing and refused money three times. The Giver ('you notice what people need and you meet it') plus the Advocate is 'kinder than his face'. It is the only place the report sees what Halyna sees.
leanings_wrong: His answers put Temper at Fiery (17/100) and When wronged at Lets them know. That describes a man who flares. The man his wife knows goes gruff and silent and bolts the door. This is a self-report limit, but the report builds both its trap and its 'worst of the four' anger on it.

He shows Takes a stand (8/100) and Keeps it in (83/100) at once, and the report never joins them. His answers could have given the real aha: he says plenty about the world and nothing about his own pain.
wording_issues: The Moralia quote 'moroseness easily slides into anger...' is used twice (type section and link 3).
'It is also the one where a little work changes the most.' is the report's own reassurance, not Gregory's. It sits right after a Gregory quote, as if it were his.

The anger cure 'Before the day starts, think through what might go wrong' is given to a man whose day already starts by checking whether his son is alive and bracing for bad news. The advice may be Gregory's, but for this man it misfires.
'Rest can feel like losing.' is unclear.
'Your strength: Counsel... You think it through well' is weak for a man who said he decides fast and fixes it later. The lean behind it (pace plus nerve = 0.33) barely clears the 0.3 cut-off.
The report never touches the war, his son, or carrying it all alone. His answers had the pieces: keeps it in, careful what he lets people see, words come hard, half waits for the catch.
best_moment: 'You said you fix things and move on. You also said you stop doing the wrong thing, but you are not one for saying sorry. Stopping is good... Something still needs saying.' For a man who quit drinking alone and told nobody, this is a true and unexpected word. The help card's 'Give me time to come round. Pressure makes me dig in' and 'Ask what I think. I rarely offer it' are also exactly him.
worst_moment: The report frames his trap as 'being right about how badly you have been treated' and labels his anger 'the worst' of the four. Then it tells him to start each day thinking through what might go wrong. Meanwhile the thing that actually shapes his days is fear for a son at the front, carried alone, and the report never says a word about it.

type_why: The Hearth fits the sensible, easy-to-be-with friend who likes company and also her hour alone with a film: 'People tend to relax around you.' The weak parts are the trap and the kindred. Her friend does not see pleasure as her snare; a sari at Onam and a film after bedtime are thin evidence. The one kindred is Antony, a desert hermit, which is an odd match for a working mother of two. His sentence also merges two separate passages of Athanasius. His friends wondered at him when he came out (Life 14, which actually says he was not 'possessed by laughter'). The cheerful face comes from a later general description (Life 67). Putting them into one moment is a small misstatement about a saint.

links.link: Lets things slide she shouldn't / calms things down when friends argue
links.why: This matches the one criticism her friend has: she goes along with her in-laws' plans to keep the peace. 'Keeping the peace can be love. It can also be the easier road' is fair and gentle.

links.link: Regrets are things never got round to / thinks about what could go wrong before something big
links.why: It is built from two answers, each only one step off centre, yet it says 'Those are one habit'. Her own strongest leaning says the opposite of 'the picture keeps you still': Hard to finish (75). She starts the walking routine every January and fades by mid-year, which is not being frozen by setbacks.

fight_should_be: Anger of the quick kind, which she and Joel would both recognise: the weekly row over the dishes, made up by morning, and being snappy on Mondays. The alternative is a plain 'nothing stands out right now'. Every private answer she gave was 'rarely' or 'sometimes'. Her one money answer was 'rarely'. Saving a little each month is prudence, not greed.
line_why: She chose the meal, and people come to her for a meal or for something explained. The Host, with Caregiver second (her parents are ageing), suits a warm Kerala household and a friend people relax around.
help_card_wrong: The card has only one line. Her help answers were clear but mild: explain why, tell me plainly, say it straight, in private, win it with a strong argument, point out everything. Each was one step off centre, which scores 0.33, just under the 0.34 cut-off, so all of them were dropped. A one-line card looks broken. A moderate answerer should still get her leanings, perhaps marked as mild.
leanings_wrong: The 'Sure of your work' note warns that the confident 'bristle when corrected'. Her answers were 'Say it straight. I can take it' and 'Point out everything. I'd rather know', and privately she rarely finds correction hard. The stock warning contradicts her.
The 'Better in public' label (33/100) reads as a charge. It comes from 'people I've just met get the best of me' plus caring what people think, which is mild and ordinary for her.
wording_issues: The quote 'Sloth is frequently looked upon as a maintenance of peace' appears twice (link 1 and the counterfeit).

'How you speak' says 'You think things through'. She answered that she sometimes says things before she has thought them through. The anger section warns her about 'what you say before it burns out', so the report contradicts itself.

Her fight is named as Greed, and its 'What feeds it' line says 'a heart with no joy inside looks for comfort in owning things'. The same report types her as Light-hearted. Said to a cheerful woman who saves a little each month, this is unfair.
'Ask someone close to you whether they agree.' (anger) hints she might hold grudges. Everything about her says she makes up by morning.
'Your strength: Counsel... The risk is that you never get round to doing it' clashes with her top leaning, Hard to finish. She gets started; she fades.
The Macarius sentence in the line section is a long stacked sentence ('Cassian names Abraham and Lot, and in his own day Macarius, who ran... and was known as...').
best_moment: 'Keeping the peace can be love. It can also be the easier road.' This gives her friend's one real concern about her in-laws, in words she can accept. Close behind is the anger section: 'Kindled reeds... The danger is the first minute: what you say before it burns out.' That is the weekly dishes row with Joel.
worst_moment: The private fight names Greed first and describes it as 'keeping a reserve, and never feeling it is enough', fed by 'a heart with no joy inside'. She is a light-hearted woman who saves a little, splurges at Onam and said privately that letting go of money is rarely hard. For an ordinary person the report manufactures a fault instead of saying honestly that nothing stands out. The one-line help card beside it adds to the sense that the report is broken.

type_why: The Spark is Luis. He is loud, warm and always moving. He starts at five and cannot sit through a meal. The trap line 'one more helping' is the sweet bread his wife hides. 'Rest can feel like losing' is his friend's 'working himself to death'. Two slips. 'You get things done' sits beside his own 'Follow-through: Hard to finish (75/100)', so the page contradicts itself. And the whole type text is word for word the one Andre got. Augustine as kindred holds up on pleasure (Confessions IV is real), but 'reading together' is an odd fit for a man who has never read a contract through.

links.link: You said you let people know on the spot. You also said you snap, and wish you had not.
links.why: This is the Saturday rush: he shouts and bangs a pot, then ten minutes later brings the cook a cold Coke. 'It is not that you do not care. It is that the care arrives too late' describes that Coke exactly. He has not put this into words. He calls it how men in his family are.

links.link: You said you tell people in charge when they are wrong. You also said your anger usually feels justified.
links.why: This is a weak top-up link. His 'anger feels justified' answer was only 'a bit'. He owns the business, so 'people in charge' points at bosses he does not have. He explains his temper as family habit, not righteous zeal. The useful sentence ('the feeling of being right is not proof') would land hard on the doctor and on his son's new ideas. The report never points it there.

fight_should_be: Gluttony, with Pride and Anger close. His friend's words are 'eating himself to death', and his doctor is talking about insulin. Pride first is defensible: he is stubborn with the doctor and with his son, and the 'start with the one you recognise most' wording is honest. The real flaw is Anger at fourth, below Vainglory. His most visible fault is the outburst, and the report's own anger section and first link treat it that way. The fight misses it because its only private anger item (y4) asks about replaying and grudges. Cassian counts the anger that 'breaks out in word and deed' and is over in an hour as its own kind (Conf. 5.11). A private item for outbursts would have caught him. Greed as the fault that troubles him least is exactly right.
line_why: Host, then Giver. The priest eats free on Thursdays. He pays for a stranger's lunch and always pays for too much of the party. This is exactly right. The Macarius line is real (Cassian, Conf. XIV.4).
leanings_wrong: Seen and unseen: balanced (50/100). The regulars and delivery men get his hugs, and his kids get his absence. His friend says 'His kids miss him'. That is 'Better in public'. He softened se1 to 'a bit', so self-report blunted it. Because of that, the counsel 'Give the people at home what strangers get' never reached him.

Little things: balanced (58/100). He never reads a contract through and ignores his glucose readings, which leans 'Easy on little things'. This one is arguable, because he does check the till and the salsa.
wording_issues: 'What you bring: ... You get things done' and 'Diligence: You keep working when others stop' sit beside 'Follow-through: Hard to finish (75/100)'. The reader sees a contradiction.
The type text and the 'Your gladness is a gift' section are word for word the same as p18's.

Anger section: 'You would probably say you rarely hold a grudge. Ask someone close to you whether they agree.' This is a stock hedge. Luis really does not hold grudges (the Coke comes ten minutes later), so it hints at a fault he does not have.
'Gregory's cure for your kind' can read as a put-down. 'For this kind of anger' would not.

Enjoys comforts: the counsel opens 'Enjoy it.' The report cannot know about his diabetes. But his friend's 'eating himself to death' makes a permission-first line risky. 'Reach for it to feel better' also misses his constant tasting, which is appetite, not comfort.
Link 2: 'Gregory would call that a pair.' This is an odd phrase that says nothing.
'pleasure borders on mirth' is a lowercase fragment dropped in after a full sentence, so it reads clipped.
Pride card: 'Last on Cassian's list, and first in its roots' is awkward. 'What takes its place: Cassian says its place is taken by humility' repeats itself.
Kindred: 'He was just as honest, later, about where his love of pleasure had led him' is comma-stacked.
best_moment: 'It is not that you do not care. It is that the care arrives too late.' This is the shout and the banged pot, then the cold Coke ten minutes later. It names a pattern he blames on his family, and his friend's 'shirt off his back, then yell at you for wrinkling it' is the same thing.
